en: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, measuring about 142,984 kilometers across its equator.
The Moon's diameter is roughly 3,474 kilometers, which is about one-quarter the width of Earth.
The Sun has a diameter of 1.39 million kilometers, making it exactly 109 times wider than Earth.
Approximately 97 percent of all water on Earth is salty water found in the five major oceans.
Diamond is the hardest known natural mineral, scoring a perfect 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
In the Philippines, a super typhoon is classified as having sustained winds of at least 220 kilometers per hour.
The most powerful earthquake ever recorded was a magnitude 9.5 event that struck Chile in 1960.
Ideal loam soil typically contains about 40 percent sand, 40 percent silt, and 20 percent clay.
Earth orbits the Sun at an average distance of about 150 million kilometers, completing one revolution yearly.
The Moon orbits Earth at an average distance of 384,400 kilometers, taking light 1.3 seconds to travel there.
The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo ejected about 10 cubic kilometers of volcanic material into the atmosphere.
